claims.text: The source preserves DFS plus a single-source shortest-path request while graph direction, edge-weight model, exact special conditions and output shape remain unspecified.

Under the declared directed nonnegative source-to-all reference contract, the exact DFS-relaxation implementation matches independent Dijkstra results over fixed boundaries and 50,000 seeded random graphs.

findings: The preserved source fixes DFS plus a single-source shortest-path request but does not preserve graph direction, edge-weight semantics, exact special conditions or whether output is one target versus all vertices.
The candidate explicitly labels its directed/nonnegative/source-to-all model as a reference contract instead of reconstructing missing source details.
The implementation does not misuse first-visit DFS as a shortest-path proof: a vertex is re-expanded whenever its distance decreases, while onPath only blocks the current recursive cycle.
An independent priority-queue Dijkstra oracle matches the exact candidate on targeted late-improvement/zero-cycle boundaries and 50,000 seeded random nonnegative directed graphs.

The answer correctly explains that BFS/Dijkstra are normally preferable and explicitly rejects negative weights and checked-distance overflow under the declared contract without fabricating project experience.
